facts.text: Fog is the best-reproduced condition for lidar, with fog chambers at CEREMA, CARISSMA and JARI providing on-road evidence.
facts.quote: Fog is the best-reproduced condition for lidar (fog chambers at CEREMA, CARISSMA and JARI)

facts.text: Fog is the best-reproduced condition for cameras, supported by SynFog on-road evidence.
Fog is the easiest condition for generative editing, according to independent on-road evidence.
facts.quote: the easiest condition for generative editing **Independent (on-road evidence)** [6, 11, 51, 93]

facts.text: Attenuation and backscatter in fog are well studied.
facts.quote: Attenuation and backscatter are well studied

facts.text: Volumetric optics for camera simulation in fog are mature.
facts.quote: For cameras, volumetric optics are mature

facts.text: Exact radiometry for cameras in fog is sensor-specific.
Radar is only mildly affected by ordinary optical fog.
facts.quote: Radar is only mildly affected by ordinary optical fog

facts.text: Moisture and multipath remain relevant to radar in fog.
facts.quote: though moisture and multipath remain relevant.

facts.text: Ultrasonic propagation under temperature and humidity effects is modelable, but supporting evidence is weak.
facts.quote: Ultrasonic propagation with temperature and humidity is modelable but weakly evidenced

facts.text: Infrared atmospheric transmission models exist for thermal cameras.
facts.quote: infrared atmospheric transmission models exist for thermal cameras

facts.text: Infrared atmospheric transmission models for thermal cameras lack off-road validation.

facts.text: Fog chamber lengths are limited—for example, to 30 m—so long-range behaviour is extrapolated for all sensors.
facts.quote: One caveat applies to all sensors: chamber lengths are limited (for example 30 m), so long-range behaviour is extrapolated [9, 11].
